headline: North-West complaint spike tracks a warehouse SLA breakdown, not a broad trend.
body: Complaints jumped mainly because North-West alone added 36 complaints, while every other region actually improved [E1]. The clearest link is WH-07's conveyor failure on June 25, which cut throughput to 60% and drove SLA breaches on North-West lanes [E6]. Multiple customers explicitly cite late deliveries against a 2-day promise as their complaint reason, including one enterprise account weighing churn [E3]. SLA percentage moved inversely with complaints over the past year, reinforcing that fulfilment delay is the operative mechanism here.

actions.driver: SLA breaches at WH-07 driving North-West complaints
actions.action: Send delay alerts and credits to North-West customers now
actions.expected_impact: Reduce complaint escalations and churn risk while SLA recovers
actions.monitoring: Track North-West complaint rate and SLA % weekly through August

what_could_change: Confirmation that WH-07 throughput has been restored, or a second warehouse showing similar breaches, would strengthen or shift this read.
caveats: Evidence covers only WH-07 events and customer complaints; root operational cause of the conveyor failure isn't independently verified.
